scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: The Connection Lab
scenes.caption: Tara arranges fictional book cards for the Connection Lab. One card is called A and has four pages, B has two, and C has six. Neel sorts the letters alphabetically, but the request was to sort by page count from smallest to largest.
scenes.speech: Tara arranges fictional book cards for the Connection Lab. One card is called A and has four pages, B has two, and C has six. Neel sorts the letters alphabetically, but the request was to sort by page count from smallest to largest.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: What changed?
scenes.caption: A sorting key is the field used for comparison. The key here is page count, so B comes before A, then C. A clear instruction also states the direction. Ascending moves from smaller to larger; descending reverses that numerical order rather than changing the meaning of the cards.
scenes.speech: A sorting key is the field used for comparison. The key here is page count, so B comes before A, then C. A clear instruction also states the direction. Ascending moves from smaller to larger; descending reverses that numerical order rather than changing the meaning of the cards.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Follow the evidence
scenes.caption: The teacher changes the data so A and B both have four pages. For this activity, equal page counts are ordered by letter, A before B. The team records that tie-break explicitly. Without a stated secondary rule, equally keyed cards could have more than one acceptable relative order.
scenes.speech: The teacher changes the data so A and B both have four pages. For this activity, equal page counts are ordered by letter, A before B. The team records that tie-break explicitly. Without a stated secondary rule, equally keyed cards could have more than one acceptable relative order.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Decide and explain
scenes.caption: A has 4 pages, B has 2, C has 6. Sort by page count, smallest first. Compare the actions, then explain which evidence supports your decision.
scenes.speech: A has 4 pages, B has 2, C has 6. Sort by page count, smallest first. Compare the actions, then explain which evidence supports your decision.
scenes.dialogue: Which order follows ascending page count?

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: Check the consequence
scenes.caption: B, A, C follows two, four, six. Alphabetical order alone ignores the supplied primary key.
scenes.speech: B, A, C follows two, four, six. Alphabetical order alone ignores the supplied primary key.
scenes.dialogue: Use the specified tie-break when keys are equal.

scenes.label: Enter the lab
scenes.title: Investigate in the lab
scenes.caption: Investigate a sorting key, then equal values, then a changed order. Test your plan, read feedback and try a changed case. Save evidence; explain one limitation.
scenes.speech: Investigate a sorting key, then equal values, then a changed order. Test your plan, read feedback and try a changed case. Save evidence; explain one limitation.
scenes.dialogue: Why does a sorting instruction need a key and sometimes a tie-break?
